name: Fathom
tagline: AI meeting recorder that summarizes calls and syncs notes to tools

pricing.notes: Official pricing checked 2026-07-30; Premium is listed at $20/user/month, annual price lower.

tiers.name: Free
tiers.limits: Unlimited recordings, transcriptions, and storage; advanced summaries, Ask Fathom, and automations are limited but no numeric public cap is stated.

tiers.name: Premium
tiers.limits: Unlimited recordings, transcriptions, and storage with the full individual AI feature set.

tiers.name: Team
tiers.limits: Minimum 2 seats; team folders, sharing, comments, keyword alerts, and CRM sync.
tiers.notes: CRM integration on individual-domain accounts is limited to 3 users; larger deployments need a team plan.

tiers.name: Business
tiers.limits: Minimum 2 seats; adds advanced coaching, deal views, security, and administration.

tiers.name: Enterprise
tiers.limits: Custom package; public price and numeric limits are not stated.
tiers.notes: Optional paid Launch Assist onboarding is available; amount is not public.

pricing.freeTierCaps: Unlimited recordings, transcriptions, and storage; advanced AI summaries, Ask Fathom, and automations have unpublished caps.
pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual; annual saves 20%-26%; 90-day money-back guarantee
pricing.hiddenCosts: Team and Business require at least 2 seats; optional Enterprise onboarding costs extra but the amount is not public.

verdictSummary: A solo clone can handle recordings, transcripts, and summaries, but the product's paid value is automated capture plus CRM/workflow sync and team sharing.
coreLoopDIY: Record or import calls, transcribe, summarize by template, clip moments, and push notes to a CRM or docs destination.
whyPeopleStillPay: They pay for workflow certainty: after every call, the right people and systems have the notes without manual effort.

priorArt.name: whisperX
priorArt.desc: Useful for transcript alignment and speaker-labeled call records.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Meetily
rejectedAlternatives.desc: A solid local meeting assistant with no turnkey note-sync integrations.

rejectedAlternatives.name: OpenWhispr
rejectedAlternatives.desc: It records, transcribes and summarizes locally, but it does not sync finished notes into the tools around your meeting.

notes: Strong 'kinda' because the core is obvious but the workflow moat is real.
prompt:
Build me a personal call-notes pipeline to replace Fathom. Requirements:

- A watched folder: I drop call recordings (m4a/mp3/mp4) into ~/Calls/inbox/,
  chokidar picks them up, a Node pipeline processes each one.
- Transcribe with whisperX for speaker-labeled, timestamped transcripts, or a
  hosted Whisper API if a key is present in .env.
- Summarize with an LLM (key in .env) using templates in ./templates/*.md. The
  default produces a 5-bullet summary, decisions, action items with owners, and
  open questions. Pick the template from the filename prefix (sales-, 1on1-).
- Clips: any transcript line can be cut into a share-able moment, ffmpeg trims
  15 seconds either side of the timestamp into ~/Calls/clips/.
- Output per call: ~/Calls/notes/YYYY-MM-DD-<name>.md, summary on top, full
  transcript below a divider.
- A small local web page (Express, localhost) listing calls with keyword search
  over transcripts.
- No accounts, no telemetry; audio never leaves my machine unless I opt into
  the hosted API.
- Out of scope: a bot that joins meetings, calendar auto-capture, CRM sync,
  team libraries. I record with my meeting app or OS and drop the file in.
- README: dependencies, keys, and how to capture system audio on macOS.
